title: Machine-learning prediction of suboptimal weight-loss response after sleeve gastrectomy
summary: An XGBoost model using eight routine preoperative predictors estimated the risk of less than 25% total weight loss one year after sleeve gastrectomy. In retrospective cohorts from three hospitals (1,094 derivation patients and external cohorts of 84 and 134), external AUC was 0.761; the paper also reports better performance than ten clinicians in its comparison. This supports risk stratification in the studied cohorts, not a causal benefit from model-guided care.
ai_technology: Six candidate algorithms were compared; an XGBoost model using eight predictors was selected and interpreted with SHAP.
organization: China-Japan Friendship Hospital; Third Xiangya Hospital; Second Hospital of Shandong University

evidence.tested: Retrospective derivation and two independent external hospital cohorts; internal AUC 0.821 and external AUC 0.761. The study compared model predictions with ten clinicians.
evidence.unknown: All cohorts were retrospective and limited to the participating hospitals; no prospective impact study established that using the model improves weight-loss outcomes.
evidence.ai_role: Six candidate algorithms were compared; an XGBoost model using eight predictors was selected and interpreted with SHAP.

source_review.scope: Primary full text and PubMed bibliographic record, including cohort design, model results and publication date.
